body: Inputs SEC XBRL (10-K 0000050863-25-000009, 0000050863-26-000011), $m; market value = cover-page public float at Q2 end (filing-sourced proxy); total liabilities = assets - equity incl. NCI. FY2024: X1 = (47,324-35,666)/196,485 = 0.0593 (x1.2 = 0.071); X2 = RE 49,032/TA = 0.2495 (x1.4 = 0.349); X3 = EBIT -11,678/TA = -0.0594 (x3.3 = -0.196); X4 = float 132,400 / TL 91,453 = 1.448 (x0.6 = 0.869); X5 = sales 53,101/TA = 0.270. Z = 1.36 (distress < 1.81). FY2023 1.91 (grey); FY2025 1.42 (distress). Book-equity Z'' FY2024 = 2.01 (grey) - the gap between book and market says the market doubted fab book values. Outcome: no default; Aug-2025 US government took ~433m new shares at $20.47 (~9.9%) by converting CHIPS grants, SoftBank bought $2bn at $23, Nvidia invested $5bn; shares outstanding 4.33bn (FY24) -> 4.99bn (Jan-2026) -> 5.32bn (Oct-2026), ~+23%. Lesson: Z measures balance-sheet distress, not the resolution path; strategic firms tend to resolve via dilution or bail-in, which still hurts existing equity.
title: Altman Z-score worked step-by-step: Intel FY2023-FY2025 (distress resolved by dilution, not default)
